correctness.rationale: The computed vertex-to-edge distinction sets for adjacent edge pairs are P_i union P_j for two page-spoke edges of matching type, and {y,a_i} union {b_j:j != i} or its symmetric {x,b_i} union {a_j:j != i} for common-spine or within-page pairs. These are all adjacent-edge pair types. Hitting every P_i union P_j requires selected non-spine vertices on all but at most one page, so at least r-1. At equality no spine vertices occur, exactly one page is empty and one non-spine vertex chosen on every other page. Orientation witnesses force counts A>=2,B>=2; these are also sufficient for hitting both oriented families. This is realizable precisely r>=5, and binary strings with at least two of each orientation give 2^(r-1)-2r choices per omitted page, hence r(2^(r-1)-2r). Independent exact breadth-first distance and edge-pair enumeration verified all candidate sets through size r-1 for r=5,6,7, yielding 30,120,350 bases. This does not replace the general proof.
